title: Retry-safe network pool creation against the SDDC Manager 9.0 API
prompt:
The `netpool` package is a dependency-free Go client for the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager network pool API. Before implementing, research `getNetworkPool` and `createNetworkPool` in `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`. Confirm their methods, paths, authentication, request and response schemas, status codes, error envelopes, and read-only fields, and cite the exact specification URLs you consulted in your final answer. Use only those two operations.

Two things are wrong in `netpool/client.go`.

First, `EnsureNetworkPool` is not safe to repeat and not safe to retry. It goes straight to `createNetworkPool`, so re-running a provisioning pass, or retrying after a failure whose outcome is unknown, either leaves a second pool behind or fails outright on a name the previous attempt already claimed. A create whose response was lost is the hard case: it may well have taken effect. Before creating, call `GET /v1/network-pools` and adopt an exact-name match with `EnsureResult.Created=false`. If no match exists, send at most one `POST /v1/network-pools`. A 201 response returns that pool with `Created=true`. After a transport failure, missing response, or 5xx response, list again; adopt an exact-name match with `Created=false`, otherwise return the original failure. If the POST returns 400 with error code `NETWORK_POOL_NAME_DUPLICATE`, list again and adopt the exact-name match with `Created=false`; if none exists, return the original error. Never send a second create request within one call.

Second, fix the create wire shape. The top-level body contains only `name` and `networks`; omit read-only `id` and `hostsCount`. Each network contains required `type`, `vlanId`, `mtu`, `subnet`, `mask`, and `gateway`, plus `ipPools` only when the caller supplied it; omit read-only `id`, `freeIps`, and `usedIps`. Each IP pool contains only `start` and `end`. An unset optional property must be absent, not empty or null.

Fix both in `netpool/client.go`, using only the standard library.

Change only `netpool/client.go`. Run `python3 tests/verify.py`; it builds and vets the module, runs the suite under `go test -race`, and checks exact request behavior, idempotent recovery, response handling, and omission of read-only and unset fields.
